t.3.68.2: Lakṣmaṇa, for his part, set the pyre alight on every side with great blazing torches, and it blazed up all around.
t.3.68.1: Thus addressed by Kabandha, those two heroes, lords of men, reached a cleft in the mountain and cast fire into it.
t.3.68.4: Swiftly shaking off the funeral pyre, the mighty one rose up like a smokeless fire, wearing two spotless garments and a celestial garland.
t.3.68.3: That huge body of Kabandha was like a great lump of ghee; as he was being cooked in his own fat, the fire burned slowly.
t.3.68.6: Standing in a shining, glory-bestowing aerial chariot yoked with swans, the greatly radiant one illumined the ten directions with his splendour.
t.3.68.5: Then, radiant and clad in spotless garments, he swiftly sprang up from the pyre with great force, overjoyed and adorned with ornaments on every limb.
t.3.68.7: Then Kabandha, having risen into the sky, spoke these words to Rāma: “Listen, O Rāghava, and I will tell you truly how you will reach the end you seek.”
t.3.68.8: O Rāma, there are six expedients in the world by which all things are weighed and considered. One who has been touched by the waning of his fortune is served by one who shares a like condition.
t.3.68.9: O Rāma, you and Lakṣmaṇa have come under an adverse turn of fate and are bereft; because of it this calamity, the violation of your wife, has befallen you.
t.3.68.10: Therefore, O best among friends, you must certainly make him your friend; for, reflecting on it, I see no success for you without doing so.
t.3.68.11: Listen, Rāma, I shall tell you: there is a monkey named Sugrīva, who was cast out by his angry brother Vālin, the son of Śakra.
t.3.68.12: On Ṛṣyamūka, the best of mountains, adorned along its borders by the Pampā, there dwells a self-possessed hero together with four monkeys.
t.3.68.13: Go quickly from here today, O Rāghava, and make him your friend; meeting him before a blazing fire, form a pact of mutual loyalty.
t.3.68.14: And Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, should not be disregarded by you, for he is grateful, able to take any form he wishes, valiant, and himself in need of an ally.
t.3.68.15: For you two are able, even today, to accomplish the task he wishes to have done; and whether he has gained his aim or not, he will do what must be done for you.
t.3.68.16: He, the son of Ṛkṣarajas, the true-born son of Bhāskara, wanders fearfully about Pampā, having been wronged by Vālin.
t.3.68.18: For that elephant among monkeys, through his skill, knows completely all the dwelling places in the world of those who feed on human flesh.
t.3.68.17: Quickly setting down your weapon, O Rāghava, make the forest-roaming monkey who dwells on Ṛṣyamūka your friend by a solemn pledge of truth.
t.3.68.19: For there is nothing in the world unknown to him, O Rāghava, as far as the thousand-rayed sun shines, O subduer of enemies.
t.3.68.20: He, together with the monkeys, will search the rivers, the vast mountains, the mountain fastnesses and the caves, and will find your wife.
t.3.68.21: And he will send forth huge-bodied monkeys to the quarters, O Rāghava, to search for that Sītā, who grieves at her separation from you.
t.3.68.22: Whether your blameless beloved has gone to the summit of Meru's peak or is lodged even in the depths of Pātāla, that foremost of monkeys will reach her, slay the rākṣasas, and give her back to you again.
